body.p: This paper is submitted as a response to the final Office Action. At the time of receiving the Office Action, claims 21-36 were pending, and claims 1-20 were cancelled. In the Office Action, claims 21-26 are allowed. Claims 27-36, however, were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Ive et al. (US 2024/0012604; hereinafter, "Ive") in view of Saur et al. (US 2018/0308451; hereinafter "Saur"), and in the cases of claims 30, 35, and 36, further in view of Samec et al. (US 2016/0270656; hereinafter "Samec").
By this paper, Applicant amends claims 27 and 30-36. No claims are presently cancelled or added, and no new matter is added.

Although claims 21-26 are allowed, the Office rejects claims 27-36 as unpatentable over Ive in view of Saur (and in some cases, in further view of Samec). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.

Notably, the Office states that Applicant's arguments were successful regarding independent claim 21, but that independent claim 27 does not contain the limitations based on which claim 21 is deemed patentable. In particular, the Office states:

claim 27 instead recites that the outward facing video display 'is see- through from the side of the user.' This implies that the display is not necessarily see-through from the side of the viewer. Claim 27 has no mention of transparency, illumination, or seeing the eyes of the wearer, and therefore remains rejected under
35 USC 103 in view of Ice and Saur supra.

In light of the Office's comments, claim 27 is herein amended to recite a therapeutic training device, comprising: eyeglass frames; an outward facing video display positioned within the eyeglass frames; and a controller coupled to the outward facing video display to control a display of media content on the video display, wherein a level of the media content is selectively adjustable such that the display of media content and eyes of a user are each selectively viewable by a patient when the therapeutic training device is worn by the user, wherein the outward facing video display is see-through from the side of the user.

This clarification shows that the device, as set forth in claim 27, differs substantially from Ive, in which the user can see only an inward-facing screen (which can display the user's surroundings, but which is not see-through to allow the user to see their surroundings directly). Similarly, although an observer of the Ive device can, in some cases, see a representation of the user's eyes on an outward facing screen, the observer cannot see the user's actual eyes, because the display is not transparent. Indeed, if the Ive device were to lose power or malfunction, the wearer would need to remove the device in order to see their surroundings or to allow observers to see their eyes.
The amendments also introduce patentable features of claim 21 (albeit, in different wording) into claim 27.

In light of the foregoing, it is Applicant's belief that the claim set as provided herein overcomes all rejections made by the Office in the Action. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that for at least the reasons provided herein, the claim set as provided herein overcomes all rejections made by the Office in the Action.
Applicant also submits that the amendments to the claims are supported by the original disclosure as filed, as evidenced by at least paragraphs [0001] and [0010] of the specification.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims are now in condition for allowance. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that a Notice of Allowance be issued in this case. Please debit any additional fees, or credit any over payment, to Deposit Account No. 50-0843. If there are any remaining issues preventing allowance of the pending claims that could be clarified by telephone, the Examiner is requested to call the undersigned attorney.
